chunks: The unbelievers would haply like to wish that they had submitted (and become Muslim).

key_terms.كَفَرُوا: disbelievers, those who cover the truth
key_terms.يَوَدُّ: to wish deeply, to desire earnestly

ai.seo_question: When will disbelievers wish they had become Muslims?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Hijr (15:2) is often interpreted as referring to the specific regret of the disbelievers of Mecca on the Day of Judgment, who will wish they had been among the Muslims (followers of the Prophet). It underscores the finality of divine decree and the contrast between the temporary ease of denial and the eternal consequence of rejection, a theme frequently discussed by scholars like Al-Tabarsi and Al-Kulayni in their tafsir works.
